title: Third-round playback and render preparation reductions
scope: Production V21 routing, channel geometry and live graph controls after the editor is open; startup excluded.

findings.change: Group admitted dependencies by destination once, replacing the complete dependency scan for every compiled vertex.
findings.evidence: Six hundred destination queries over six hundred dependencies reduce destination reads from 360000 to 600; incoming entries retain authored order and reference ownership.
findings.limitations: Invocation-local graph preparation; no global cache admits mutable dependencies. Existing independent PDC oracle checks sidechain, nested, inactive-rack and consumer offsets.

findings.change: Group enabled programme routes by output once and compute each maximum directly, removing per-output whole-edge filters and mapped latency arrays.
findings.evidence: The actual production compiler passes with whole-edge filter projections forbidden. Index checks preserve output and edge order and exclude disabled routes.
findings.limitations: This is the explicit V21 path solve, distinct from the earlier legacy track/bus latency map construction. Shared projection and maximum work is one finding.

findings.change: Use a minimum heap for the ready frontier instead of shifting and sorting the whole array after every newly ready vertex.
findings.evidence: Thirty-two independent DAG fixtures retain exact former UTF-16 lexical order; a 601-vertex actual compiler fixture passes with Array.sort forbidden. Cycle refusal remains unchanged.
findings.limitations: Heap construction and traversal are still required; tests establish order and removed sorting, not a per-change Electron latency estimate.

findings.change: Resolve track sidechain destination widths from a build-local membership/width snapshot rather than finding the track for every edge.
findings.evidence: One hundred track identities are read once; one hundred repeated sidechain queries add zero authored reads. Orphan width entries retain the former empty-ID fallback.
findings.limitations: Preparation owns detached width values for one build. Rebuilding reflects changed values; first-match and direct lookup comparisons cover malformed duplicate inputs outside persisted admission.

findings.change: Resolve mixer-node and mixer-sidechain widths from one first-match index instead of merging groups, sends and cues and scanning them for each edge.
findings.evidence: The observed mixer width is read once; one hundred repeated queries add no reads or merged-array projections. Group-before-send duplicate precedence and missing-node refusal remain exact.
findings.limitations: Accepted graph facts are immutable during a build; unrelated rebuilds do not reuse this snapshot.

findings.change: Index output widths once rather than find-scanning all outputs for each destination edge.
findings.evidence: One hundred repeated output queries read zero authored fields after the single initial width read; direct destination parity and missing-output TypeError checks pass.
findings.limitations: The benefit scales with output count and fan-in; the factory still prepares each output once.

findings.change: Use one group identity set for ADM terminal and meter-bank classification instead of scanning every group at each call.
findings.evidence: One hundred repeated terminal/classification queries add no group identity reads. Group/send labels match the original classifier and terminal records remain independently frozen.
findings.limitations: The same membership cost serves both production callers and is counted once.

findings.change: Prepare VCA gain products by member once, removing each strip's repeated scans of every VCA and its memberships.
findings.evidence: Four hundred repeated strip/master/absent-member queries add zero member reads. Products keep exact authored multiplication order, duplicate membership applies once, mute gives zero, and excluded master gives one.
findings.limitations: One immutable graph build owns the products; graphs without VCAs use a constant resolver.

findings.change: Index effect lane addresses by strip and effect once rather than scanning all lanes and creating a key set for every suspended slot.
findings.evidence: Five hundred lane addresses are read once; registering twenty effect targets adds no lane reads and preserves exact original suspended descriptors. Existing disabled/bypassed/rack-disabled and master-bypass graph tests pass.
findings.limitations: Descriptor inventory admission and registration order remain authoritative; no suspended target is made active.

findings.change: Retain each known runtime strip's solo audibility for later mute automation evaluations instead of repeating routing reachability traversals and solo-array allocation.
findings.evidence: After initial track/master queries, two hundred repeated audibility queries add zero Set.has traversal visits. Existing all-silent-route, solo topology and graph automation regressions pass.
findings.limitations: Only the finite owned strip set is retained; unknown keys are evaluated without retention. No-solo or ignored-solo graphs use constant true resolvers.
